name: Google Shape;57;p11
text:
Write Once,
Run Anywhere

name: title-context
text: High-level, class-based, object-oriented language developed by Sun Microsystems in 1995.
textPreview: High-level, class-based, object-oriented language developed by Sun Microsystems in 1995.

text: Java is one of the most popular programming languages in the world. It is secure, reliable, platform-independent, and suitable for both beginners and professional developers.

name: TextBox 4
text: How Java Works

name: execution-summary
text:
- Source code is saved in a .java file.

- javac compiles source into bytecode.

- The JVM executes bytecode for the OS.

- The same bytecode runs on any compatible JVM.

text:
Source
Code

text: Output

name: jdk-heading
text: Core Components

name: jdk-body
text:
- JDK: tools to develop Java programs
- JRE: environment to run Java applications
- JVM: engine that executes bytecode
textPreview: - JDK: tools to develop Java programs | - JRE: environment to run Java applications | - JVM: engine that executes bytecode

text: The JVM is the main reason Java is platform-independent. We compile a Java program once, and the generated bytecode can run on any operating system containing a compatible JVM.

name: TextBox 4
text: Basic Structure

name: structure-lead
text: Every Java application starts from the main method inside a class.
textPreview: Every Java application starts from the main method inside a class.

name: code-text
textPreview: public class Main { |     public static void main(String[] args) { |         System.out.println("Hello, Java!"); |     } | }

name: program-parts-heading
text: Program Parts

name: program-parts-body
text:
- class Main declares the class
- public allows access
- static runs main without an object
- void means no return value
- String[] args stores command-line input
textPreview: - class Main declares the class | - public allows access | - static runs main without an object | - void means no return value | - String...

name: data-types
text: Data types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean, String, arrays, classes, interfaces, and objects.
textPreview: Data types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean, String, arrays, classes, interfaces, and objects.

text: Every Java application starts execution from the main method. Variables store information, and data types define what kind of information can be stored.

name: Title 1
text: Object-Oriented Programming

name: oop-intro
text: OOP organizes programs around classes and objects so code is easier to reuse, protect, and maintain.
textPreview: OOP organizes programs around classes and objects so code is easier to reuse, protect, and maintain.

name: encapsulation-heading
text: Encapsulation

name: encapsulation-body
text:
- Combines data and methods inside a class
- Protects data using access modifiers
textPreview: - Combines data and methods inside a class | - Protects data using access modifiers

name: inheritance-heading
text: Inheritance

name: inheritance-body
text:
- Allows one class to acquire another class's properties and methods
- Supports code reuse
textPreview: - Allows one class to acquire another class's properties and methods | - Supports code reuse

name: polymorphism-heading
text: Polymorphism

name: polymorphism-body
text:
- Lets one action behave in different ways
- Common examples: overloading and overriding
textPreview: - Lets one action behave in different ways | - Common examples: overloading and overriding

name: abstraction-heading
text: Abstraction

name: abstraction-body
text:
- Hides unnecessary implementation details
- Shows only essential functionality through abstract classes and interfaces
textPreview: - Hides unnecessary implementation details | - Shows only essential functionality through abstract classes and interfaces

name: oop-lead
text: OOP makes Java programs reusable, secure, modular, and easier to maintain.
textPreview: OOP makes Java programs reusable, secure, modular, and easier to maintain.

text: OOP represents real-world entities as classes and objects. Its four main pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

name: TextBox 5
text: Control Flow and Data

name: decision-heading
text: Decision-Making

name: decision-body
text:
- if-else chooses a branch using a condition
- switch selects between fixed cases
textPreview: - if-else chooses a branch using a condition | - switch selects between fixed cases

name: loops-heading
text: Loops

name: loops-body
text:
- for, while, and do-while repeat code
- enhanced for-each iterates through collections
textPreview: - for, while, and do-while repeat code | - enhanced for-each iterates through collections

name: methods-arrays-heading
text: Methods and Arrays

name: methods-arrays-body
text:
- methods package reusable logic
- arrays store multiple values of the same type
textPreview: - methods package reusable logic | - arrays store multiple values of the same type

name: mini-code
textPreview: if (marks >= 40) { System.out.println("Pass"); } | for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { System.out.println(i); } | static int add(int a, int b)...

text: Conditions help a program make decisions, loops repeat tasks, methods improve code reusability, and arrays store multiple values of the same type.

name: TextBox 4
text: Applications and Conclusion

name: apps-heading
text: Where Java Is Used

name: apps-body
text:
- Android, web, backend, and enterprise systems
- Banking, e-commerce, cloud, big data, desktop, IoT, and DSA
textPreview: - Android, web, backend, and enterprise systems | - Banking, e-commerce, cloud, big data, desktop, IoT, and DSA

name: advantages-heading
text: Advantages

name: advantages-body
text:
- Easy to learn, portable, secure, robust, and object-oriented
- Garbage collection, multithreading, libraries, frameworks, and community support
textPreview: - Easy to learn, portable, secure, robust, and object-oriented | - Garbage collection, multithreading, libraries, frameworks, and communi...

name: limits-heading
text: Limitations

name: limits-body
text:
- Can be slower than C/C++ and may use more memory through the JVM
- Syntax can be lengthy, and Java is not ideal for low-level system programming
textPreview: - Can be slower than C/C++ and may use more memory through the JVM | - Syntax can be lengthy, and Java is not ideal for low-level system ...

name: tools-heading
text: Frameworks and Tools

name: tools-body
text:
- Spring Boot, Hibernate, Maven, Gradle, JUnit, Tomcat
- IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, and NetBeans
textPreview: - Spring Boot, Hibernate, Maven, Gradle, JUnit, Tomcat | - IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, and NetBeans

name: closing-line
text: Java is a complete development platform for learning fundamentals and building real-world applications.
textPreview: Java is a complete development platform for learning fundamentals and building real-world applications.

text: To conclude, Java is not only a programming language but also a complete development platform. Its portability, security, object-oriented structure, and wide industry usage make it excellent for students and professional developers.
